page: Microsoft Azure D4s_v4 is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the DSv4 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 2 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8272CL processor with an x86_64 architecture. The CPU operates at a base clock speed of 2.6 GHz and is equipped with 32 KB L1d cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 35 MB L3 cache. It supports advanced instruction sets including AVX, AVX512F, and AVX512_VNNI. The instance is configured with 16.0 GB of system memory, providing 4.0 GB per core. It does not include local storage or bundled GPUs, though it is Premium Storage capable.

Performance benchmarks indicate average single-core capabilities but weaker multi-core scaling. The stress-ng single-core CPU test scores 1410.29, and Geekbench single-core reaches 1171.0, both falling into the average category. However, multi-core performance is weaker, with a stress-ng multi-core score of 3705.66 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 2604.0. Memory bandwidth is a notable bottleneck, with uncached read speeds dropping to 17.74 GB/sec and uncached write speeds at 15.28 GB/sec. This translates to weaker performance in memory-intensive workloads, as seen in the multi-threaded bzip3 decompression score of 16.46 GB/sec and Redis SET operations at 3.41 million operations per second.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the D4s_v4 offers a balanced resource density for standard workloads that do not require high-speed local NVMe storage or heavy multi-threaded compute. Given its dedicated CPU allocation and average single-thread performance, it is suitable for general-purpose workloads such as light web serving, basic text processing, and small-scale application hosting. It can also handle lightweight LLM text generation using small models, where it achieves an average speed of 94.04 tokens per second. However, it is less suitable for database operations, software compilation, or memory-bound tasks due to its weaker multi-core and memory bandwidth profiles.

Running on Microsoft Hyper-V, this x86_64 instance features AVX-512 support but lacks local storage and GPU accelerators. Benchmarks show average single-core performance, with a stress-ng single-core score of 1410.29, but weaker multi-core and memory bandwidth results, including an uncached read speed of 17.74 GB/sec. Qualitatively, the instance provides a balanced resource profile for standard workloads without demanding high-throughput memory or local disk I/O. It is best suited for general-purpose applications, light web serving, and small-scale text processing tasks.
